## About
I'm a second-year MPH candidate in Epidemiology at the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health, where I'm also pursuing a certificate in Applied Biostatistics and Public Health Data Science. My work sits at the intersection of epidemiologic methods and health policy, with a focus on how data can be used to identify and address gaps in access to care.
Before Columbia I spent three years in a clinical setting as a lead medical assistant in dermatology and as a clinical research assistant at the University of Chicago Medicine — which shaped how I think about the distance between what the data say and what patients actually experience. I'm currently looking for roles in healthcare consulting.

## Interests
- Health equity and access to care
- Health policy, including social determinants of health and disability policy
- Infectious disease epidemiology
- Reproducible analysis in R and Python
